title: Week 3 Analysis
subtitle: Everybody just had their worst week of the season.
intro_paragraphs: Three weeks in, and for the first time this season every single bettor's total went down, not up. The standings didn't just shift — they scrambled hard enough that nobody's picks kept pace.

fun_facts.heading: A Bad Week for Everyone
fun_facts.body: Every one of the seven bettors lost ground this week, from Dustin's -21 (landing on 21, already in last) to Dilger and Cadegn's matching -41 — the two biggest drops in the pool. Tom is still in first at 37 points, but only because a -27 week was less bad than what happened to everyone chasing him. Hume fell the hardest among the leaders, dropping 35 points to land in 2nd.

fun_facts.heading: A Dead Tie at the Middle, a Real Gap at the Top
fun_facts.body: Mike T and Farmer are tied exactly — 24 points each, the first true tie the pool has had. Tom's lead over 2nd place is the widest gap on the board at 7 points, which after this week's carnage counts as a comfortable margin.

fun_facts.heading: The Locks Just Took Their Worst Hit Yet
fun_facts.body:
Only 2 of the 8 preseason unanimous picks are still holding, down from 5 last week. The AFC North locks that survived two straight weeks — Pittsburgh third, Cleveland fourth — both broke as the division scrambled into a four-way 2-1 jumble. New England also lost its hold on second place in the AFC East to the Jets.

One pick has now held for three weeks running without interruption: Buffalo first in the AFC East, the only preseason lock nobody's touched. On the other end, the Rams — the pool's most unanimous pick to win the NFC West — still haven't led that division once in three tries.

closing_paragraph: Nobody's season is decided by three weeks of this much chaos — the locks keep breaking and the leaderboard keeps flipping. Same time next Tuesday.
